name: arc-fill-alternating-row-gaps
description: Use when an ARC grid contains same-color markers in rows separated by one background cell. Fill the gaps with the contrasting color.
---

# Fill alternating horizontal gaps

## Trigger
Use when a demonstration shows repeated marker cells in a row with exactly one background cell between neighboring markers, and the output fills those intervening cells with a new color while leaving all other cells unchanged.

## Procedure
1. Compare the input/output demo cell-by-cell to establish the transformation: for each row, detect horizontally adjacent-in-pattern marker cells (same marker color, exactly one cell apart with a single background cell between them).
2. Change only the single intervening background cell to the demonstrated fill color. Keep marker cells, all other background cells, and grid dimensions unchanged.
3. Apply the inferred rule to the test grid. In the Continual-ARC example, markers were color 3 on background 9 and gaps became 2; the test used markers 1 on background 0, so the same rule made each gap between horizontal 1s color 2.
4. Do not fill vertical gaps, gaps longer than one cell, or background cells not bracketed horizontally by matching markers in the same row.
5. Check the completed grid row-by-row, preserving every original non-gap cell, then submit the grid.

## Pitfall
Some rows contain multiple marker groups or a marker at the edge; only fill an actual single-cell gap bracketed by markers on both sides. A lone marker or an unbracketed background cell is unchanged.

description: Use when ARC rows show repeated markers with single-cell gaps.
---

# Fill alternating horizontal gaps

## Trigger
A demonstration shows repeated marker cells in rows with exactly one background cell between neighboring markers. The output fills those intervening cells with a contrasting color and leaves everything else unchanged.

## Procedure
1. Compare the demo input and output cell-by-cell. Identify the marker color, background color, and fill color.
2. In the test grid, scan each row. For each background cell with matching marker cells immediately to its left and right, replace it with the fill color.
3. Preserve all marker cells, other background cells, and the original grid dimensions. Do not fill vertical gaps, longer gaps, or unbracketed cells.
4. Verify each changed cell was horizontally bracketed by same-color markers and that no other cell changed.
5. Submit the full transformed grid.

## Example
In the solved example, demo rows used marker color 3, background 9, and fill color 2. The test used marker color 1 and background 0; the same inferred fill color 2 was placed between horizontally bracketed 1s.

## Pitfall
Rows can contain multiple separate groups, and some markers can be unpaired. Only fill a single cell that is immediately bracketed on the same row by matching markers.
